# Seeds whose SELF-HOST x86-64 result disagrees with the interpreter's, for
# TestDifferential_SelfHostX86_64 (internal/e2e/diff_oracle_selfhost_test.go).
#
# Format: <seed> <reason + issue>. Blank lines and # comments ignored.
#
# A row is a KNOWN COMPILER BUG being tolerated so the rest of the corpus keeps
# running — not a seed that is allowed to be wrong. The leg fails on a NEW
# divergence and equally on a LISTED seed that starts agreeing, so this list
# prunes itself as the bugs are fixed rather than becoming somewhere they are
# forgotten.
#
# For every row here the interpreter, native x86-64 and native arm64 agree with
# each other; that agreement is what says the self-host compiler is wrong rather
# than the generated program being invalid.
#
# THE LIST IS EMPTY. Every seed the leg can compile now agrees with the
# interpreter. Keep the file — an empty list is the strongest form of the gate,
# since any divergence at all fails the leg — and keep the record below of what
# left, because it is what the next round of probing should be measured against.
#
# Measured 2026-08-06 over seeds 0..511 (the leg's default corpus), after #6272:
# 325 agree, 0 diverge, 187 compile gaps. Count the gaps, not just the
# agreements, when reading a run: the leg only proves what it could COMPILE, so
# a fix that turns a wrong answer into an IR bail raises the gap count while
# looking like a win in the divergence column.
#
# That caution cuts both ways, and the last five runs went the other way: 204
# agree / 308 gaps, then 263 / 249 (#6237 + #6246), 291 / 221 (#6261), 311 / 201
# (#6268), 325 / 187 (#6272). One bail can cost far more than the seed that exposes it — an
# if-expression whose branches are 64-bit took the whole MODULE off the IR path,
# and fernsmith emits if-expressions everywhere, so a single missing branch in
# one classifier was suppressing a tenth of the corpus.
#
# CENSUS OF THE 187 GAPS, so the next round is aimed rather than sampled. The
# first split is by the reason FERN_STRICT_IR=1 gives:
#
#   78  function value <fn>$clo not defined   → #6256. NOT one mechanism — the
#                                               issue's own comments record that
#                                               correction: several shapes share
#                                               this message, and grouping by
#                                               message is what made the first
#                                               reduction fix the wrong thing.
#                                               Now the LARGEST pile, and it GREW
#                                               by 7 across #6268 without anything
#                                               about it changing: seeds that used
#                                               to stop earlier now get far enough
#                                               to reach it. Read a moved number
#                                               as a reordering before a
#                                               regression.
#   13  call to unknown symbol T.to_string    → a method call on a bare type var.
#   96  no reason string                      → see the second split below.
#
# The no-reason pile used to be the least actionable: the strict-IR message
# names the FUNCTION it gave up in and nothing else. It does not need the message
# widened, though — the bail site is recoverable from the BINARY. Build the
# self-host compiler with symbols and break on the failure constructor:
#
#   ./bin/fern -g -target x86-64 -o /tmp/fsh-g examples/self_host/fern.fern
#   break *__method_irlower__LowerState_fail
#   commands
#     silent
#     info line *(*(unsigned long *)$rsp)
#     cont
#   end
#
# gdb attributes the line to "fern.fern", but the NUMBER is a line in whichever
# module the containing symbol names (irlower__* → irlower.fern) — read the
# symbol, not the filename. There is normally exactly one hit per compile, so
# the reading is unambiguous, and the whole 96 profile in a few minutes.
#
# That gives the second split, measured after #6272. Line numbers go stale on
# the next edit to irlower.fern — the FUNCTION name is the durable half:
#
#   40  lower_stmt_inner :13660  the `return`-width guard: a width-64 value
#                           returned from a 32-bit return type. It has never been
#                           a real wide return — every cause found so far is a
#                           false width READING upstream, and each was a different
#                           classifier: #6261 a u32-suffixed literal past i32-max
#                           (94 → 51), #6272 a match-EXPRESSION taking its IIFE
#                           return type from the first arm alone (54 → 40). Treat
#                           a hit here as "which classifier lost the width", not
#                           as a returned value that is genuinely too wide.
#   24  lower_value_block :11865  the wide-tail deferral #6268 added — a 64-bit
#                           if / match tail in a value block, held back because
#                           wasm miscompiles it (#6267). Removing the gate does
#                           not change the gap TOTAL (measured 201 either way):
#                           these 24 fail again downstream, so the gate is where
#                           they stop, not why.
#   21  lower_i64 :6739 / :6809
#    8  lower_iife_match :13246  the payload-bindable gate.
#    3  lower_expr :10354 / :10876
#
# So the 187 are three piles, not a fog: 78 sharing the $clo message (#6256, the
# largest, and being reduced separately), 64 in two lowering sites, 45 over five
# more. Two entries have drained since this census began: #6268 took
# lower_value_block's non-`return` tail (61) to nothing, #6272 took the width
# guard 54 → 40. Re-measure before picking — draining one pile reshuffles the
# others, as the $clo count moving 71 → 78 for free shows.

# CRASHES — the self-host-compiled binary died by SIGSEGV where the interpreter
# returned a value. These were ONE bug: #6207, a `Map { … }` literal whose keys
# the parser could not classify, building itself string-keyed so map_set
# compared integer keys through __fern_str_eq. Eight rows left with it —
# 200 / 228 / 455 with the two classifiable key forms (#6213 leaf-reachable
# arithmetic, #6220 cast targets), then 59 / 97 / 144 once the fix stopped being
# syntactic and read the `Map[K, V]` declaration instead. Every crash row in the
# corpus was that bug; the header used to hedge that the survivors might be "a
# different cause (or causes)", which was true of what had been measured at the
# time and false once they were reduced.

# WRONG VALUES + ARENA EXHAUSTION — both sections emptied together, because they
# were ONE bug. infer_expr_width classified a number literal by MAGNITUDE alone,
# so a small suffixed literal (`7i64`) read as 32 bits and every 64-bit value
# derived from one was computed at the wrong width. Fifteen rows left with that
# fix: 4, 20, 28, 29, 48, 52, 99, 117, 123, 241, 324, 362, 364, 375, 482. The
# old note here — that the interp=0 rows were "worth checking as a group before
# reducing them one at a time" — was right; 117's "arena exhausted" was a
# symptom of the same mis-widening, not a separate leak.
#
# Seed 502 left in two steps. #6228 first moved it from a silent wrong answer to
# an IR bail (`FERN_STRICT_IR: __lam_22`) — the safe direction, but a gap rather
# than a fix — and #6237 then closed the bail, so it now compiles and agrees.
#
# The cause was NOT irt_guess, which this note used to name and which cost an
# hour to rule out. A lifted if-EXPRESSION gets its return type from
# `if_expr_rt` at PARSE time, and because that writes a non-EMPTY "i32",
# infer_ret_types_module never revisits it — so irt_guess never runs on these
# lambdas at all. Teaching irt_guess the suffix AND the magnitude changes
# nothing; measured, twice. `if_expr_rt` was the fourth literal classifier in
# parser.fern and the last one that read neither.
#
# The hole PREDATED the width work either way: a big-magnitude branch
# (`if (c) { 5000000000 } else { … }`) bailed identically before #6228, with no
# suffix involved.

# Also gone earlier, with their own fixes: 121 / 265 / 365 (#6177, the maps
# runtime need-gate).
